title: cl_interpreter
description: How the CL compiler is invoked. This file is the contract every CL toolchain implementation must satisfy: same entry point, same arguments, same exit codes. Implementations may be Python, Rust, Lean, or otherwise; the calling convention is fixed.
name: cl

v0_python.notes: First-cut compiler. Lives at cards/tool/cl_compile/python.py once written. Reads a .cl source file, emits target code per --target.

positional.name: source
positional.description: Path to a .cl source file (or '-' for stdin).

options.description: Path to a JSON file matching cl_compilation_model schema's hardware field. If absent, the compiler probes the host: arch, os, cores, gpu_present.
Write the resolved IR (cl_ir schema) to this path alongside the target code. Useful for tooling and audits.
Where to write target code. May be a file or '-' for stdout.
Stop after typecheck; do not emit. Exits 0 if the program typechecks.
Set a feature flag in the ResolveContext, e.g. --feature-flag use_simd=true.

exit_codes.3: resolve error (no variant satisfies the context)
exit_codes.5: I/O error (source not found, output not writable)

examples.description: Emit Python from a CL source.
Multi-target emit driven by per-decl overrides.
examples.command: python3 cards/tool/cl_compile/python.py pipeline.cl --target python --hardware hw_lab.json --emit-ir pipeline.ir.json --out build/

determinism: For a fixed (source, --target, --optimize, --hardware, --feature-flag*) tuple, the compiler MUST produce byte-identical output. Two runs that disagree are a bug.
